newsitem.title: FRANCE: Douwe Egberts France raised retail prices.
newsitem.headline: Douwe Egberts France raised retail prices.

text.p: Douwe Egberts France said on Wednesday that it had raised retail prices for its arabica coffees by some 20 percent in line with higher futures prices.
The decision was taken in the second half of February and the price increase will be effective for consumers between mid-March and mid-April.
"We told our clients that there would be a rise of 20 percent on arabicas but nothing on robustas yet," chairman Pascal Jouannet told Reuters.
Douwe Egberts France is the French unit of Dutch coffee roaster Douwe Egberts, part of the Sara Lee Corporation of the United States.
Douwe Egberts controls 15 percent of the French coffee market.
Jouannet did not say if the company planned a second round of price increases following the latest surge in coffee prices.
But he said that most coffeee roasters were not adequately covered, leaving them more vulverable to price fluctuations.
"The stock situation is extremely tight," he said.
He said roasters had been operating with stocks of eight to 12 weeks but were now working with less.
Earlier Kraft Jacob Suchard said it had raised retail prices of its arabicas by nine francs per kilo, effective February 24.
Tight stocks sent New York May arabica futures above $2.00 per pound on Wednesday. --Dominique Vidalon, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
